newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Attorney General seeks bond probe with SEC.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Attorney General seeks bond probe with SEC.

text.p: California's Attorney General plans to investigate several local bond transactions following state Treasurer Matt Fong's call for a probe, according to officials and a letter released on Friday.
M. David Stirling, chief deputy state attorney general, said in a letter to Fong that his office had also contacted the Securities and Exchange Commission to coordinate a joint investigation.
In September, Fong called on the SEC and California's Attorney General to investigate nine municipal securities transactions underwritten by Pacific Genesis Group Inc.

In these municipal bond deals, Fong alleged that illegal payments of bond proceeds were made, bond proceeds were used to retire private debts and bond professionals failed to identify the actual project beneficiaries.
"In my view, these practices violate state laws, raise federal securities law concerns and harm the interests of the issuer community in general," Fong said in September.

The transactions were conducted under the state's Marks-Roos Local Bond Pooling Act, authorizing the formation of joint powers agencies to finance the capital projects of local governments in California.

"The Attorney General shares your concern that these bond deals warrant an investigation into whether or not those involved have exceeded the legitimate limits of the Marks-Roos Act and perhaps federal securities laws as well," Stirling said in his letter to Fong, dated September 25.

"We have assigned this matter to the government section and it has already been in contact with the SEC regarding a joint investigation," Stirling told Fong. "We will keep you informed of this matter as it progresses."
The Attorney General's government section reviews local and state government matters.
The Attorney General's office released a copy of Stirling's letter on Friday.

The SEC has also responded to Fong's call for a probe of the deals, but the SEC and Fong's office have refused to release a copy of that letter. Sources said the SEC referred Fong's request to its municipal enforcement officials.
